concepts.title: The Letter and Its Context
concepts.definition: The text is an excerpt from My Daughter, My Friend by Irene Chua - a letter dated 19 June 1995 written by a mother to her teenage daughter Ming, sharing her deepest thoughts and celebrating the special bond between mother and daughter.
concepts.key_idea: A letter across generations: a mother writes not to instruct but to befriend.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe108.txt letter excerpt and its introduction

solution_steps.explain: Irene Chua writes to her teenage daughter Ming.
The epistolary form makes the thoughts personal and permanent.
The letter shares life insights and affirms the bond.

concepts.title: Theme - Following Your Dream
concepts.definition: The central message urges the daughter - and every reader - to follow that dream: to identify what one truly loves, work towards it bravely, and not let fear or others' expectations dim one's own path in life.
concepts.key_idea: A dream followed with courage is the surest route to a self-owned life.
concepts.textbook_ref: iebe108.txt passages on dreams and life advice

solution_steps.explain: Identify your dream and pursue it with courage.
Fear, comparison and others' expectations can dim dreams.
The reader is invited to apply it personally.

concepts.title: Epistolary Style and the Mother-Daughter Bond
concepts.definition: Being a letter, the text shows epistolary features - salutation, intimate first-person voice, reflections dated in time and a personal sign-off; its tone is warm, honest and reflective, modelling how trust can turn a parent into a friend.
concepts.key_idea: Letter form plus warm voice equals a heart-to-heart on paper.

solution_steps.explain: Date, salutation, intimate voice and closing signature.
Warmth, honesty and reflection colour every paragraph.
The letter turns a mother's advice into a friend's companionship.
